title: Introduce operator-proof catalog and KMS locality enforcer
author: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Context: We currently rely on per-request RBAC checks and a general audit pipeline, but operator access patterns across regions lack deterministic evidence for residency decisions and post-hoc compliance reviews. This PR introduces two coordinated features: 1) an operator-proof catalog (OPC) — a compact registry of signed operator access assertions and their provenance that surfaces during policy evaluation; and 2) a KMS locality enforcer — a middleware that validates KMS key locality against tenant residency claims and annotates audit envelopes when a locality mismatch is resolved.

Motivation: Several recent compliance reviews and audits revealed gaps where operator actions could be executed via stale operator credentials or cross-region operator sessions without a canonical claim in the audit trace. The OPC provides an immutable, signed assertion referenced by RBAC v2 decisions. The KMS locality enforcer prevents keys from being used in unintended regions and records the enforcement rationale in a tamper-evident audit envelope.

High-level design: OPC is a small service (service/opc) that stores signed operator assertions: operator id, role template, scoping (geozone), issuance time, and optional approval tokens. Assertions are minted by the operator-approval flow and are signed with a platform signing key; the policy engine fetches a short-lived proof when evaluating decisions. The KMS locality enforcer plugs into the kms client path (pkg/kms/guard) and cross-checks the key location against the tenant's pinned-region header and the OPC scoping claim. When an enforcement decision is made, the enforcer appends a compact proof entry to the audit envelope (audit/enrichers/locality.json) including a hash pointer to the OPC assertion and the KMS metadata.

Behavioral guarantees: - RBAC v2 decisions that depend on operator-scoped assertions are denied if no OPC proof is presented unless the request comes from an explicit operator-exempt route (documented). - KMS locality checks produce deterministic deny/allow decisions; allow decisions record a proof, denies produce a sanitized audit record and an operator-level alert.

Migration and rollout plan: - Feature-flagged behind ff.opc and ff.kms_locality. - Phase 1 (canary): enable in staging and 5% of traffic for dedicated accounts for 2 weeks; collect metrics (latency, deny-rate, proof-miss-rate). - Phase 2 (shadow): run checks in shadow mode for all regions to build profiler data and operator assertion coverage. - Phase 3: opt-in enforcement for enterprise tenants, followed by global enforcement after policy signoff.

Testing and verification: Added unit tests for the signature verifier, integration tests that simulate cross-region operator sessions, and an e2e compliance test that asserts that the audit envelope contains the locality proof when a KMS call is allowed. Load tests show a median 0.4ms added latency on the KMS call path under normal conditions.

Related work: builds on ENG-1188 (rbacv2 policy templates) and complements the new audit-envelope-v3 (PR #564738). Linear references: ENG-2029 (OPC design), SEC-87 (KMS locality requirements).

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc linked and reviewed by security
- [x] Unit + integration tests added
- [x] Feature flags in place
- [x] Migration/runbook drafted under docs/compliance/opc-migration.md
- [x] Observability: metrics and tracing spans added

Impact and risk: The change touches authz and KMS hot paths; risk is mitigated by flags, canary rollout, and a fast rollback path (feature flag kill-switch). No breaking changes to public APIs.

Release notes: Introduces operator-proof catalog (OPC) and optional KMS locality enforcement to improve residency proofing and audit fidelity. Enterprise customers can opt-in before global enforcement.

Implementation notes (concise): - service/opc: store + sign assertions using platform key (pkg/crypto/sign). Assertions are compact (protocol buf artifact) with an indexed hash. - pkg/policy/opa_adapter: fetch OPC proof in EvaluateRequest; cache proof for 30s to avoid extra roundtrips. - pkg/kms/guard: validate key region against tenant header and OPC scoping claim; annotate audit envelope via audit/enrichers/locality.go. - cli/rbacctl: new subcommand rbacctl proof inspect <assertion-hash> to fetch human-readable assertion for ops.

Security considerations: All OPC assertions are signed and stored encrypted at rest. The OPC service requires an additional operator-approval scope; assertions are TTL-bound and revocable. Audit envelopes include only compact proof references (hashes + reason) to avoid exponentiating sensitive payloads.

Documentation: docs/compliance/opc-overview.md and docs/platform/kms-locality-runbook.md added; rbacctl docs updated.

review_thread:
Ben Whitaker: 'Design looks strong; want to understand cache staleness risk for OPC proofs when operator assertions are revoked.'
Aisha Kapoor: 'We implemented TTL + revocation marker: policy engine consults revocation index when a proof is older than 30s; added tests to cover revocation path.'
Marta Li: 'Please ensure the audit envelope does not leak key material or operator tokens.'
Aisha Kapoor: 'Audit entries only contain proof hash, KMS region, and enforcement rationale; added explicit assertion to the docs and an automated linter that fails if PII-like fields are present in the enricher output.'
Omar Hernandez: 'Can we add a non-disruptive mode where we record deny reasons but allow the call for 48 hours?'
Aisha Kapoor: 'Added shadow mode (ff.kms_locality=shadow) per request; comments updated with rollout steps.'
Approvals: Ben Whitaker approved after two iterations; Marta Li approved. Omar requested one small doc change which was addressed.
